thesis: Amazon is the largest AI infrastructure builder in the world and is being penalised for it. Q2 2026 net sales hit $200.6B (+20%) with AWS accelerating to 36.7% growth ($42.2B, 39.4% segment margin) behind a $496B contracted backlog, while advertising grew 26%. The cost is ~$220B of 2026 cash capex, which has pushed trailing free cash flow to an outflow of $7.6B and will push reported FY2027 EPS below FY2026 as depreciation lands. At $246 the stock trades ~14% below its 52-week high and ~25% below the $321-331 analyst consensus: the demand is contracted, the returns are deferred to 2028.

drivers: AWS sustains 33%+ growth as the $496B contracted backlog converts; 2027 capacity already reserved
Trainium and Graviton5 give AWS a structural cost-per-token advantage; AI and chips each already above a $25B annualised run rate growing triple digits
Capex peaks in 2027 and free cash flow inflects sharply positive in 2028 against a far larger revenue base
Advertising compounds above 20% off a $19.8B quarterly base, aided by Alexa for Shopping and Ads Agent
Unmodelled optionality from Amazon Leo, Zoox paid robotaxi service, Amazon Supply Chain Services, and the Anthropic stake

base_case.assumptions: AWS decelerates gradually from 37% toward the high-20s, consolidated operating margin holds near 13%, 2027 capex plateaus rather than falling, and free cash flow returns to modestly positive in 2028. Reported EPS is flat to down in FY2027 (~$10.47 consensus) before resuming growth. Lands near the low end of the $321-331 analyst consensus range.

risks: AI capacity demand digests while ~$220B of 2026 capex is already sunk; trailing FCF stays negative
Depreciation on $446B of net property and equipment compresses consolidated operating margin back toward 10%
AWS growth slows toward 20%, repeating the FY2025 pattern when it grew 19.7% versus Google Cloud at 35.8%
The $53.4B pre-tax Anthropic mark partially reverses, making reported EPS comparisons sharply negative
Market re-rates Amazon as a capital-intensive infrastructure business; the $196.00 52-week low sits inside this band

catalysts.event: Expanded FTC Prime settlement refunds begin reaching additional Prime customers
Q3 2026 results (expected ~29 October, not company-confirmed); AWS growth print is the swing factor for the thesis
Holiday quarter; Amazon Leo initial satellite internet service from a ~400-satellite constellation; Zoox paid robotaxi ramp after NHTSA Part 555 exemption
Q4 and FY2026 results plus first formal 2027 capital expenditure framing
Potential Anthropic liquidity event or further mark-to-market revaluation of the stake (press speculation, not company-guided)

key_risks: Capital intensity: ~$220B of 2026 cash capex has driven TTM free cash flow to negative $7.6B from positive $25.9B six quarters ago
Depreciation wave on $446B of net property and equipment; consensus FY2027 EPS (~$10.47) sits below FY2026 (~$12.88)
Reported earnings quality: Q2 2026 EPS of $5.75 included $53.4B of pre-tax Anthropic marks; comparable EPS was ~$1.88
AWS competitive and demand risk; a single decelerating quarter with capex still climbing would validate the bear case
Memory and component cost inflation was explicitly cited in raising capex guidance from $200B to $220B
Regulatory: FTC Prime billing settlement, ongoing marketplace antitrust scrutiny, and agentic-commerce access disputes
Consumer and macro exposure across ~79% of sales, plus an ~80bp unfavourable FX impact embedded in Q3 guidance
Long-term debt nearly doubled to $128.9B in H1 2026 as the build became partly debt-funded
